_comment: Reference coverage: how many of the references a document lists are actually
cited in its body.  A document that lists N references normally cites nearly
all of them, so a low coverage means the body's citation markers were lost —
not that the author cited nothing.
This is the only signal that catches a SILENT parse failure.  The orphan count
cannot: an orphan is a citation without a source, and a citation that was never
detected in the first place cannot be orphaned.  A .txt of a paper that cites by
superscript parses to zero markers, zero claims and ZERO ORPHANS — the plain-text
format carries no superscript information, so 'in all cases.35' is just a number.
Measured on the corpus: healthy parses sit between 76% and 100%; parses whose
markers were eaten sit at 0-33%.  The threshold below is set inside that gap.
min_references: below this many references the ratio is meaningless (a paper with
two entries citing one of them is 50% and perfectly fine), so no warning is made.
